name: fourstream_example
description: Classic four-stream chemical process (two reactor feeds and products), loads in MW. Illustrates the tool on a non-food process with high-temperature demand.
reference: University of Oklahoma, ChE design course notes 'Minimum Utility', Example 1.1 (stream data and targets).

provenance.eta_lorenz: assumed, same value as the brewery case (Padullés et al., 2026)
provenance.source_T_C: assumed: 130 °C, below the pinch (T* 145 °C), where the process rejects heat
provenance.sink levels: assumed, illustrative: 160 °C (commercial range) and 200 °C (upper end of IEA HPT Annex 58 scope)
provenance.basis: none: the source gives no operating hours
provenance.ambient_T_C: assumed: not given by the source
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: from the overall U of the University of Oklahoma notes (equal split)

economics._note: No economic data in the source. Prices: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1 for the consumption band at 8000 h/year; heat pump investment: Danish Energy Agency catalogue by sink temperature (≤60, ≤125, ≤150 °C); other parameters: tool defaults (Sources page). All are assumptions for this case.

hp_dea_1_1.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 1.1 'Heat pump, up to 60 °C, temp. lift 40 K': 0.95 M€/MW (0.91-0.95), unit size 0.5-5 MW

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged)

sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The source plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's Portuguese context. Bands at 8000 h/year: gas 255,600 GJ/year (I4); heat pump electricity 6,400 MWh/year (ID; site total unknown). Bands change with the hours: gas I3 (10,000-99,999 GJ) = 0.0512, I4 (100,000-999,999 GJ) = 0.0445; electricity ID (2,000-19,999 MWh) = 0.1135, IE (20,000-69,999 MWh) = 0.0897
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity (see cost_functions); replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect costs (new hot-water piping, 0.19-0.23 M€/MW) not included

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: University of Oklahoma ChE design notes 'Units and Area Targeting' (same example): overall U = 0.001 MW/(m2 K) = 1 kW/(m2 K) for every match; split into equal film coefficients of 2 kW/(m2 K) so that 1/U = 1/h_hot + 1/h_cold (lecture notes, not peer-reviewed). Utility-side coefficients take the same value

cost_law.label: Towler 2020 U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel), bare (F = 1)
cost_law.source: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Table 6.6, U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel), Ce = 24,000 + 46 S^1.2 USD (USGC, Jan 2007, CEPCI 509.7), valid 10-1000 m2; x CEPCI 797.9/509.7 (2023; Chem. Eng. Sept 2024 p. 45) / 1.0816 USD/EUR (ECB, 2023)

cost_law.label: Towler 2020 U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel) x 3.5 (Hand factor, installed)
cost_law.source: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Table 6.6, U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel), Ce = 24,000 + 46 S^1.2 USD (USGC, Jan 2007, CEPCI 509.7), valid 10-1000 m2; x CEPCI 797.9/509.7 (2023; Chem. Eng. Sept 2024 p. 45) / 1.0816 USD/EUR (ECB, 2023); x 3.5 Hand installation factor for heat exchangers (Table 6.3)

area_targeting._cold_utility: cold utility cost not included (no source): TAC is a lower bound

basis_hint: No operating hours are published. 8000 h/year lies within the 90-95 % attainment typical of continuous plants (Sinnott and Towler, 2020, Sec. 1.3.1: 7,880-8,320 h/year).
